newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Italy CPI must fall under 3pct for rate cut - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy CPI must fall under 3pct for rate cut - Fazio.

text.p: Inflation must fall to under three percent year-on-year for the Bank of Italy to cut rates, central bank governor Antonio Fazio said.

"To lower the discount rate, the goal is to get inflation to drop below three percent in 1996," Fazio told a press conference after the gathering of European Union Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors in Ireland on Saturday.
Italian Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi added, at the same press conference, that by the end of 1996 inflation would certainly be under the three percent level.

However Fazio warned: "Official rates can only be lowered when markets are ready for them, otherwise it can be counterproductive. Long term rates must drop first, and short term rates can then follow."

Italian inflation was 3.4 percent year-on-year in August. Provisional price data for September is due on Monday and Tuesday. The Bank of Italy last moved rates on July 23, when it cut its discount rate to 8.25 percent from 9.0 percent.
Both Ciampi and Fazio stressed that a "serious and rigorous" 1997 budget bill was essential in the process of securing necessary market credibility to allow Italian interest rates to drop further.

The 32.4 trillion lire deficit-cutting budget is expected to be unveiled at the end of this week. "We are working on it, have a bit of patience until Friday," Ciampi told reporters who asked for details of the package. --Alma Davanzo, Rome Newsroom +396 6782501
